{{ElectionsMA}}
The '''2026 Massachusetts gubernatorial election''' is scheduled to take place on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Massachusetts]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Maura Healey]] is seeking a second term. She faces [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Michael Minogue in the general election. It is one of 39 gubernatorial elections occurring nationwide in 2026, and one of 18 in which the incumbent governor is seeking another term.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elections |url=https://www.nga.org/governors/elections/ |access-date=2026-10-05 |website=National Governors Association}}</ref> 

[[Primary elections]] took place on September 1, 2026, where incumbent governor Maura Healey won the Democratic nomination running unopposed, and Mike Minogue won the Republican nomination against Brian Shortsleeve.<ref>{{cite news|last=Shook|first=Ashley|date=September 22, 2025|title=Massachusetts legislature approves 2026 primary election date|url=https://www.wwlp.com/news/massachusetts/massachusetts-legislature-approves-2026-primary-election-date/|work=[[WWLP]]|access-date=September 24, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolman |first=Jordan |date=2026-09-02 |title=Minogue wins GOP primary for governor, setting stage for matchup with Healey |url=https://commonwealthbeacon.org/politics/minogue-wins-gop-primary-for-governor-setting-stage-for-matchup-with-healey/ |access-date=2026-10-05 |website=CommonWealth Beacon |language=en-US}}</ref>

In the run-up to the general election, Republican candidate Mike Minogue spent $6.1 million in September 2026 on his election bid, making it the most expensive gubernatorial race in Massachusetts history. Minogue outspent the 2006 Republican nominee and former Lieutenant Governor [[Kerry Healey]], who spent $4.4 million in the run-up to the [[2006 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|general election]] versus [[Deval Patrick]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Buskirk |first=Chris Van |date=2026-10-02 |title=GOP nominee Michael Minogue spent a record $6.1 million last month |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/02/metro/minogue-61-million-spending-september-governors-race/ |access-date=2026-10-05 |work=The Boston Globe |language=en-US |issn=0743-1791}}</ref>

== Background and policy issues ==
The 2026 gubernatorial race is taking place in the midst of the second Trump presidency. Major themes in the general election center around affordability and the cost of living in Massachusetts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scalese |first=Roberto |date=2026-08-20 |title=Here's who's running for Mass. governor in 2026 |url=https://www.wbur.org/news/2025/10/17/2026-massachusetts-governor-candidates |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=www.wbur.org |language=en}}</ref>

=== Immigration and ICE ===
During her first term, Healey had been a vocal critic of the [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administrations]] actions relating to immigration and [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]] agents, and signed the Protect Act in August 2026 which aimed to provide limitations on ICE arrests in courthouses, schools, child care programs, nursing homes, and non-public areas of healthcare facilities, among others.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manning |first=Jacqueline |date=September 8, 2026 |title=Governor Healey Issues PROTECT Act Guidance for Health Care Providers, Employers, Law Enforcement and State Agencies |url=https://www.mass.gov/news/governor-healey-issues-protect-act-guidance-for-health-care-providers-employers-law-enforcement-and-state-agencies |access-date=October 5, 2026 |website=Mass.gov}}</ref> 

Mike Minogue campaigned in support of the Trump administration's actions relating to immigration enforcement, pointing to a reduction in [[fentanyl]] overdoses in the wake of increased arrests and deportations. He supports the deportation of illegal immigrants residing in the United States, but reiterated the focus should be on illegal immigrants who are violent criminals. "Nobody should be afraid to leave their home, go to school or the hospital. I’m going to make sure that that doesn’t happen".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-02 |title=Mike Minogue makes case for Mass. governor bid: More affordability, fewer ICE raids |url=https://www.wgbh.org/news/politics/2026-10-02/mike-minogue-makes-case-for-mass-governor-bid-more-affordability-fewer-ice-raids |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=GBH |language=en}}</ref>

=== Energy costs ===
Going into the fall of 2026, home heating oil prices were approximately 70% more expensive in Massachusetts compared to the previous winter, with approximately 20% of homes in the state using fuel oil as a method of home heat.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gandhi |first=Hazel |title=Heating oil costs just hit their highest level in years. Winter is still months away. |url=https://www.capecodtimes.com/story/news/local/cape-cod/2026/09/27/mass-heating-oil-prices-increase/91903839007/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Cape Cod Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Massachusetts Home Heating Profile |url=https://www.mass.gov/info-details/massachusetts-home-heating-profile |access-date=October 5, 2026 |website=Mass.gov}}</ref>

On October 5, 2026, Healey signed an executive order to declare a "state of energy emergency" heading into winter months to alleviate increased home heating costs, which she attributed to the [[Iran war (2026-)|Iran war]]. "I’m looking at ways to provide relief to people right now. Trump’s got to end this war. Trump’s got to end this war. That’s got to be job one right now”.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff And Wire Reports |date=2026-10-05 |title='Energy emergency' fires up Massachusetts governor's race |url=https://www.bostonherald.com/2026/10/05/energy-emergency-fires-up-massachusetts-governors-race/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Boston Herald |language=en-US}}</ref> The executive order aimed to provide home heating assistance for approximately 50,000 [[Middle class|middle-class]] homes using oil to heat and increase the benefit that had been in place for 150,000 [[Poverty|low-income]] homes, as well as the state paying SMART charges, which incentivizes [[Solar panel|solar]] adoption.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sesselman |first=Jamy Pombo |date=2026-10-05 |title=New actions to lower winter energy bills for Mass. residents announced |url=https://www.wcvb.com/article/gov-maura-healey-announcing-new-actions-to-lower-winter-energy-bills/74028047 |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=WCVB |language=en}}</ref>

In the run-up to the general election, Minogue called for a statewide emergency relating to home heating costs, as well as repealing state climate taxes. “I’ll cut energy bills by a third by eliminating climate taxes that have nothing to do with how much energy you actually use. I’ll abolish the unfunded, unenforceable [[Net-zero emissions|Net Zero]] mandate".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff And Wire Reports |date=2026-10-05 |title='Energy emergency' fires up Massachusetts governor's race |url=https://www.bostonherald.com/2026/10/05/energy-emergency-fires-up-massachusetts-governors-race/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Boston Herald |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Debates ==
On October 8, 2026, a televised debate occurred on [[WBZ-TV]] between Maura Healey and Mike Minogue.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gross |first=Samantha J. |date=2026-10-08 |title=Healey, Minogue clash in first of two governor's race debates |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/08/metro/healey-minogue-debate-wbz-tv-governor-race/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |work=The Boston Globe |language=en-US |issn=0743-1791}}</ref>{{toclimit|3}}
